findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Wixams Station capital project carries £33m impairment risk pending government decision
findings.detail: The council received £33m Exceptional Financial Support specifically for Wixams Station risk. The council is building a two-platform station but costs may not contribute to a planned new four-platform project. Assessment of potential impairment awaits Department for Transport decision, creating material uncertainty on a major capital commitment.
findings.matters: A potential £33m capital write-down would severely impact the balance sheet and net asset position. Uncertainty depends on external government action, creating reporting risk and financial planning instability.
findings.figures: £33m EFS approved for Wixams Station; impairment assessment pending DFT decision
findings.quote: A further £33 million was approved to manage the risk relating to the Wixams Station, as costs incurred in building the two-platform station may not contribute to the new four platform project. The Council is awaiting information on the new station from DFT to assess the potential impairment.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Children's Services overspend crisis: 30% budget overspend with peaked demand
findings.detail: Children's Services overspent by £14.3m in 2025/26 (30% of service budget). Looked-after children peaked at 306. Reductions achieved in 2024/25 'were not maintained', indicating no sustained early help or prevention strategy. A targeted program to reduce residential placements is stated as underway but timing and success unproven.
findings.matters: Children's placements are typically the largest demand pressure in local government. An overspend of 30% signals the council has lost operational control and lacks effective early intervention preventing children entering care.
findings.figures: Children's Services £14.3m overspend, 30% of service budget, 306 looked-after children at peak
findings.quote: Children's Services ended the year £14.3 million overspent, equal to 30% of the Children's budget. Reductions in the number of children in our care seen in 2024/25 was not maintained, and currently the number of looked after children stands at a peak of 306.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Unmanageable structural budget deficit persists through 2029/30
findings.detail: The council forecasts a £27m budget gap in 2027/28 and cumulative £58.6m gap by 2029/30. Medium-Term Financial Strategy was not agreed during the year. Even with the planned improvement plan and savings, the structural deficit remains. Current projections show no clear path to eliminating government dependency.
findings.matters: Forecasted deficits this large cannot be closed by normal efficiency savings. They signal need for service reductions, asset sales, or ongoing exceptional support—all indicating governance failure.
findings.figures: £27m gap 2027/28, £58.6m cumulative gap by 2029/30, £18.9m savings target for 2026/27
findings.quote: We will continue to face financial challenge in the coming years, with a budget gap of £27m in 2027/28 and a cumulative gap of £58.6m by 2029/30. Sound financial governance is a critical priority, requiring all areas to work together to manage demand and deliver savings.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Reserves depleted to £14.2m, below recommended minimum, with no clear recovery path
findings.detail: Usable reserves fell to £14.2m at 31 March 2026, below the risk-assessed recommended range. The council's own Section 151 Officer recommended rebuilding reserves within two years (March 2027), but with a £27m budget gap in 2027/28 and £58.6m cumulative gap to 2029/30, this is increasingly unrealistic.
findings.matters: Depleted reserves leave no buffer for demand shocks or unexpected pressures. Once exhausted, the council has no financial flexibility and cannot manage service disruptions.
findings.figures: Usable reserves £14.2m, budget gap £27m in 2027/28, cumulative gap £58.6m by 2029/30
findings.quote: Usable reserves are £14.2 million at 31 March 2026. We continue to face financial challenge in the coming years, with a budget gap of £27m in 2027/28 and a cumulative gap of £58.6m by 2029/30.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Dependency on £58m exceptional support to avoid Section 114 Notice
findings.detail: The council received £22m Exceptional Financial Support for 2025/26 and requires £58m for 2026/27 (£25m revenue, £33m for Wixams Station risk). Without this government support, the council would have issued a Section 114 Notice. This dependency masks structural deficits that cannot be addressed without continued exceptional support or service cuts.
findings.matters: A lender cannot rely on repeated exceptional government support as sustainable funding. The council is operationally insolvent without government handouts, indicating the improvement plan has not yet stabilised the underlying position.
findings.figures: £22m EFS 2025/26, £58m EFS 2026/27 (£25m revenue + £33m Wixams Station)
findings.quote: Following discussions with MHCLG the Council applied to the Government for Exceptional Financial Support for 2025/26 of £20 million plus £2 million relating to Cleat Hill to avoid issuing a Section 114 Notice.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 2025-26 - final draft 13 July 2026
findings.headline: Failed savings plan and massive overspend in 2025/26
findings.detail: The council set a £10.5m savings target but achieved only £5m (48%), resulting in a £17.7m overspend. Children's Services alone overspent by £14.3m (30% of its budget), driven by external placements and agency staffing. This pattern indicates structural inability to control spending in demand-led services.
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence the council can deliver savings plans. Achieving only 48% of target while overspending signals deep operational control failures and unreliable financial management.
findings.figures: £10.5m savings target, £5m achieved, £17.7m overspend, Children's Services £14.3m overspend (30% of budget)
findings.quote: The savings target for 2025/26 was £10.5 million, of which £5 million was achieved. The overspend for the 2025/26 financial year is £17.7 million.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The Wixams station project changed strategic direction following announcement of a competing Universal theme park development
findings.detail: In Autumn 2024, the Wixams station project moved to construction phase but then changed strategic direction following announcement of a Universal theme park development. The council is being supported by accounting advisors on this project, and audit work is ongoing for 2025-26. The nature and financial impact of the strategic change are not detailed in this report.
findings.matters: Major capital projects carry execution risk and can consume significant resources. Mid-project strategic pivots suggest planning challenges and may indicate sunk costs or need to revise project scope and budget.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The council incurred significant unfunded costs from the October 2024 gas explosion emergency response
findings.detail: A gas explosion in Bedford on 19 October 2024 killed two people and required evacuation of residents. The cause was a gas leak during heat pump drilling of naturally occurring underground gas. The council faced substantial financial costs for emergency response and recovery efforts. The auditor reviewed the council's response arrangements and raised no concerns, but the incident created unplanned demand on the budget.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted emergency costs reduce financial flexibility and may consume reserves. This demonstrates external shocks to which the council is exposed. Combined with existing financial stress, this limits ability to absorb further unexpected costs.
findings.figures: Incident 19 October 2024; specific costs not quantified in report
findings.quote: The council faced significant financial costs due to the emergency response and recovery efforts following the incident.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The savings programme required to bridge the budget gap depends on delivery of transformation and demand management initiatives that have not been fully embedded
findings.detail: The 2025-26 budget assumed achievement of £10.4m efficiency savings identified across four themes. The Section 25 Report from the s151 officer noted the budget contained risks and would require close management. The auditor concluded there was a significant weakness because the Improvement Plan was not fully embedded in council operations as of March 2025, only being formally approved in January 2026.
findings.matters: If planned savings are not delivered, the budget position worsens immediately. Transformation and demand management are inherently uncertain and dependent on management execution. The late establishment of the Improvement Plan suggests weak advance planning.
findings.figures: £10.4m efficiency savings assumed in 2025-26 budget; £18.0m savings required in 2025-26 to maintain balanced budget position
findings.quote: The budget assumed the achievement of £10.4m of efficiency savings, which were identified across four themes highlighted within the Council efficiency plan with each theme having a series of specific identified savings schemes. The Section 25 Report from the s151 officer highlighted that the budget contained risks within the assumptions and that it would require close management in order to be achieved.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: Property valuations and fixed asset records lack audit evidence and reconciliation to financial statements
findings.detail: For Investment Property, the auditor selected 10 items for testing but evidence was not provided for 3 of them, and floor area evidence was missing for all items. For Property, Plant & Equipment, the Fixed Asset Register did not reconcile to the financial statements, preventing sample testing until reconciliation was completed. These are material asset categories that required further work scheduled for the 2025-26 audit.
findings.matters: Unreconciled property and fixed assets represent potentially material misstatements in the balance sheet. Without evidence of proper valuation and reconciliation, the reported asset values cannot be trusted. This affects net asset position and borrowing capacity calculations.
findings.figures: 3 of 10 investment property samples lacked evidence; Fixed Asset Register unreconciled to financial statements
findings.quote: Whilst audit evidence was shared for the majority of items sampled evidence was not provided for 3 out of 10 items selected. Initial audit review identified that the Fixed Asset Register did not reconcile directly to the financial statements.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The finance team lacked sufficient capacity to meet statutory deadlines and audit obligations, causing delays in publishing financial statements
findings.detail: The council did not publish its unaudited financial statements by the 30 June 2025 statutory deadline because the initial draft was not of sufficient quality. The auditor identified this as a significant weakness: the finance team had insufficient capacity to undertake core objectives and respond to additional demands. Despite new appointments after year-end, the team remains stretched due to high demand for financial information. Some key reconciliations (payroll and Fixed Asset Register) required further work before audit could proceed.
findings.matters: Weak finance function capacity affects financial controls, timeliness of reporting, and audit quality. This compounds the audit risk, delays access to financial information needed for decision-making, and signals internal control deficiencies.
findings.figures: 30 June 2025 deadline missed; statements published July 2025; payroll and FAR reconciliations required rework
findings.quote: The financial statements were not published in line with the 30 June 2025 deadline due to the initial draft set of accounts not being suitable for publication. Whilst new appointments have been made to the team since the end of the financial period the finance team are still stretched.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The council had to request £90m of Exceptional Financial Support from MHCLG to prevent insolvency
findings.detail: Facing the projected overspend, Bedford requested £90m across three financial years (2025-26 to 2027-28) from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. The requests for 2025-26 and 2026-27 were approved in principle on 23 February 2026. This requirement was only identified after the financial year ended, indicating plans developed during the year proved inadequate.
findings.matters: Exceptional Financial Support is a last-resort intervention used when a council cannot balance its budget. It signals the council lacks sufficient resources or cost control and depends on central government bailout. This materially affects the council's financial standing and independence.
findings.figures: £90m requested across 2025-26 to 2027-28; approved in principle 23 February 2026
findings.quote: The Council have submitted a request to MHCLG for Exceptional Financial Support totalling £90m across the three financial periods up to and including 2027/28 – the requests for the periods 2025/26 and 2026/27 were approved in principle on 23 February 2026.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: The council faces a projected £42.2m funding gap by 2029 and an £11.7m overspend in 2025-26 that would fully deplete available reserves
findings.detail: The September 2024 Medium-Term Financial Strategy forecast shows revenue spending will exceed available resources by £42.2m by the end of 2029 without additional action. In 2025-26, the council was forecasting a £11.7m overspend (by September 2025) against available general fund reserves of only £11.1m. This would fully exhaust reserves. The council has usable reserves have declined 44% since March 2022 (a £39.9m reduction).
findings.matters: A council that depletes reserves lacks a buffer for emergencies or volatility. The multi-year structural deficit signals the council cannot sustainably balance its budget and will require external support or service cuts. This is a clear solvency risk for lenders.
findings.figures: £42.2m gap by 2029; £11.7m September 2025 overspend; £11.1m available reserves; 44% reduction in usable reserves since March 2022
findings.quote: In September 2024, the Council updated the Medium-Term Financial Strategy for the four years to 2028/29. This report estimated that, without additional action, the gap between revenue spending and resources will grow to £42.2m by the end 2029. This is a clear risk to financial sustainability given the level of reserves available to the Council.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - Appendix A - Auditor’s Annual Report for Bedford Borough Council 202425
findings.headline: Auditor issued a disclaimer of opinion on the council's financial statements, unable to obtain sufficient audit evidence on multiple critical areas
findings.detail: The auditor could not gather sufficient evidence to sign off on the financial statements before the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026. Key areas where evidence was unavailable include Property, Plant & Equipment valuations, Investment Property valuations, Employee benefits expenses, reserve movements, and comparative figures for 2024. This is the second consecutive year of disclaimer.
findings.matters: A disclaimer means the auditor cannot verify the accuracy of the council's reported financial position. This creates material uncertainty about the balance sheet and reserves available, directly affecting creditworthiness assessment and covenant compliance.
findings.figures: Disclaimer issued 26 February 2026; areas affecting £billion-scale assets and reserves unverified
findings.quote: We issued a disclaimer of opinion on the Council's financial statements on 26th February 2026. This is because we were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence over the financial statements.
